standard.title: ISO 14971 — risk management clauses, mapped by clause title only
standard.scope_note: The standard text is paid. Only clause numbers and titles are public (ISO OBP table of contents), and that is all this file quotes, so every row is verbatim=false and no row may be carried. Five of the ten clauses are mapped; the rest are not, because a risk-management process is engineering work and listing it as 'partial' would only pad the table.

rows.reason: A package can hold the file's documents, name each by digest, and prove none changed since sealing - which is what makes a file auditable. What is missing: whether the file contains the right records, in the required structure, traceable to hazards.
Scope, responsibilities, acceptability criteria and the overall-residual-risk method are authored by the manufacturer. A record layer can store the plan as evidence; it cannot write or judge it.

rows.id: ISO 14971 5.4 Identification of hazards and hazardous situations
rows.reason: Hazard identification is the analytical core of the standard. No check in this library invents hazards, and pretending to enumerate them from a package would invert the whole point.

rows.id: ISO 14971 7.2 Implementation of risk control measures
rows.reason: Implementation happens in the product. What a package can show is that a verification result was recorded against a control - not that the control is in the shipped software, and not that it works.

On the tampered fixture the probe exits non-zero and names the entry whose digest no longer matches - which is the shape of a post-production signal being caught rather than absorbed. The demo re-verifies a package after it was sealed and catches a substituted key, which is the shape of a post-production signal. What is missing: a real collection channel - complaints, literature, other devices on the market - and the review that decides whether a signal is safety-relevant.
